text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Aviation sources say regulator Federal Airport Authority of Nigeria has impounded an aircraft belonging to Air Gabon following the airline's failure to pay 26 million naira debt for landing and parking charges at Lagos international airport.
- Mousa Booth, spokesman for state power company National Power Electric Authority (NEPA), says a debt of 12 billion naira owed it by consumers is responsible for its erratic power supply nationwide.

- The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group has put on hold construction of a $450 million project to improve crude oil storage and exports at the Forcados Terminal because of tribal clashes since March in nearby oil town Warri, paper says, quoting own investigation.
- Nigeria's military government has approved a budget of two billion naira for a project aimed at controlling the recurring surging of the ocean from the Lagos Bar Beach onto land.
- DN Meyer, a subsidiary of tyre makers Dunlop, threatens legal action against Lagos state tax authorities for sealing its premises last week over alleged failure to pay company tax.
- Colonel John Dungs, military administrator of Delta state overseeing the oil town of Warri, says he has given a final warning to locals to end the clashes there.
- Nigerian military government has introduced a new insurance law which allows individuals to hold 100 percent equity in insurance companies against 25 percent previously.

- Cletus Iromantu, head of telecommunications sector regulator Nigerian Communications Commission, quotes its survey as showing the banking industry as the most-computerised of all sectors in the country.
